items.summary: We give an explicit convex polygon with 63 rational vertices whose area, after its shortest closed Euclidean billiard length is normalized to one, is smaller than that of Mallée’s parabolic triangle. This disproves Conjecture 2.2 of Balitskiy, Mitrofanov and Polyanskii (2026). The polygon was found by moving supporting lines near the parabolic triangle’s focal contacts and then discretizing the resulting shape. The proof checks the literal polygon in exact rational arithmetic: 63 width directions and all 39,711 triples of supporting edge lines. A three-file verification package contains the coordinates and an independent checker. The result identifies a better competitor, without claiming that it is optimal.
items.title: A rational polygonal counterexample to the Mallée parabolic triangle conjecture

items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. items.summary: Classical metaphysics treats the mutual exclusivity of alternatives as primitive: or, in its physical reading, excludes by nature. This paper argues the polarity should be reversed. Exclusivity is an achievement — stated, interior, structural content of the alternatives them-selves — rather than an intrinsic feature of disjunction; and once exclusion is relocated from the exterior of or to interior content, a new composition regime falls out with no further postulation: the joint regime, in which co-present alternatives simply decline to carry mu-tual negations. The difference between the regimes is fixed by a one-statement test, which answers the suspicion of mere notation; a strict fence separates what the new primitive sup-plies (openness) from anything its occupants might do with it (use), which blocks the two natural misreadings; and the primitive itself receives a deflationary definition: or-jointness is the logic-valued regime of not stating mutual negations on the interior side — obtained by declension, not addition. We argue the proposal reclassifies the color-exclusion problem that fractured the Tractatus, and supplies the determinable-based literature on metaphysical indeterminacy with the composition story it has lacked. A documented fact about the direction of discovery then bears on the proposal’s status: the two composition forms were first extracted, in companion work, from the case-by-case structure of interference phenomena — before the present philosophy existed — so the dichotomy’s shape is explained by what it was extracted from, not by any philosophical purpose it might serve. Whether the world instantiates the joint regime is the companion framework’s proposal, on which no thesis here leans; what the provenance establishes is that the primitive was not gerrymandered for the argument that now exposes it.
items.title: Exclusivity as Achievement: Relocating Mutual Exclusion to the Interior, and the Logical Primitive That Falls Out

items.summary: The laws of physics are CPT-symmetric, yet laboratory quantum mechanics prepares the past and only samples the future. This working paper distinguishes five levels of taking the symmetry seriously — symmetric laws with the open future left implicit, a two-boundary description, symmetric processes, a nontrivial final boundary, and laboratory access to it — places published views and experiments on them, and states what each predicts for a final-boundary test, in which an engineered terminal acts on a flag and an entangled partner is read on every trial. Exact results: an open future propagates backward through any physical channel; a terminal can only transfer, never manufacture, final-side contrast, giving lambda = tanh(hbar omega / 2 k T_f) in a swap model, the mirror of a reset; a clamp of budget A needs an energy of at least k T_f ln A in some branch; under free local control any every-trial final condition signals, with visibility equal to the clamp strength. Under stated transfer models a null reads as a lower bound on a swap-equivalent final temperature (Partridge: above 3.5e7 K for escaping microwaves; planned qubit tests: about 27 K and 360 K). The paper audits transport to the future, specifies what any physical source of a final condition must supply, and finds that no named candidate meets the specification. CPT motivates the reversed-resource question; channel duality bounds its possible transfer; laboratory access remains an additional physical hypothesis, decided only by experiment. No new experimental result is reported. Drafted with AI assistance and revised after AI-assisted reviews; responsibility rests with the author.

items.summary: Berggren's three matrices generate the tree of primitive Pythagorean triples and preserve the quadratic form x₁² + x₂² − x₃². Cha, Nguyen and Tauber (2018) built such trees for other integral ternary forms Q of signature (2,1). We ask whether the matrices alone determine Q. Main results: Recovery criterion (Theorem 3.1). A set of isometries of Q determines Q up to scale exactly when no nonzero vector is sent to plus or minus itself by all of them. Equivalently, the group they generate is not virtually abelian; for integral isometries, it acts irreducibly. The proof is elementary linear algebra and applies to arbitrary real groups. Berggren trees (Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.3, Remark 3.5). Any two generators determine Q in Berggren's tree and in each of the five trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber. The definition of a Berggren tree alone does not force this: the generators A and A² give a Berggren forest for x₁² + x₂² − x₃² whose two generators both yield edges but do not determine Q. Roots at a rational null line (Theorem 3.6). For a primitive null vector P with divisor G, the minimum of Q on (P^⊥ ∩ ℤ³) \ ℤP is S = |det(2J)|/(2G²). An explicit congruence, Gm ≡ −τ (mod S), decides which minimal vectors e + mP are roots. N-cusps (Theorems 3.7–3.8, Corollary 3.9). For Q = ax₁² + bx₁x₂ + cx₂² − Nx₃² with D = b² − 4ac < 0, all data at the null vectors (p, q, 1) are explicit. A minimal root exists there if and only if gcd(G, S) divides D/G, and in particular whenever D is cube-free. Recovery by integral reflections (Theorem 3.12, Proposition 3.13). Minimal roots at two or three distinct rational null lines yield three integral reflections that determine Q. The paper also relates the reflections in the trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber to minimal roots (Remark 3.17), and states an open question for trees produced by their construction.
items.title: The Inverse Berggren Tree Problem

items.summary: The Visibility Problem Hypershape Shadow Hypothesis II   Chloe J. Tully https://orcid.org/0009-0007-5661-7332 HSH Paper 1 https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23010822 Project UAP Studies   v0.1 3 October 2026 Preprint. Not peer-reviewed.   Companion to HSH I (28 September 2026). Tier-2 material is not in this paper.     DISCIPLINE   HSH I derived a geometry and assumed a flux law. This paper keeps the geometry and splits the assumption. What is proved is proved about the toy model. What is not selected — a coupling, a bulk metric, a relativistic completion — is named and left open. Neural coupling and retrocausality are still excluded. They are not implied by anything below.     ABSTRACT   HSH I predicted a parabolic light curve by taking received flux proportional to the area of the brane slice. That step is not geometry. For a 4-ball translating along the hidden axis, orthographic area scales as ρ² and reproduces the parabola F₂ = 1 − (t/τ)². Uniform emission through the 3-volume of the same slice scales as ρ³ and produces F₃ = [1 − (t/τ)²]^(3/2). The families meet at onset, peak, and end, and disagree in the shoulders: at |t/τ| = 1/√2, F₂ = 1/2 while F₃ = 1/(2√2). Calibrated photometry can tell them apart.   A 4-ellipsoid at fixed orientation in the XW plane stays inside both families, for every line of sight. An orientation that changes during the transit need not. One computed counterexample is given. The C₅ cover twist proposed in open problem O5 — cross-edges (i, 0) ↔ (i+1, 1) in place of the self-steps — is isomorphic to the untwisted cover, so the 1/φ gap is unchanged. No uniform self-step weight puts the even sector on the five-value spectrum flagged in HSH I. Coupling remains the critical open problem. Ansätze are stated with kill criteria. None is adopted.     CONTENTS   1. What HSH I already fixed 2. Two measures, two light curves 3. Fixed orientation stays parabolic 4. The C₅ twist does not close O5 5. Coupling ansätze, none chosen 6. What this does not unlock 7. Status of claims

items.summary: This chapter develops the research programme of Generative Relational Economics (GRE) by translating the conceptual, methodological, and substantive architectures developed earlier in the book into a cumulative, contestable, and revisable programme of inquiry. Its principal concern is answerability: GRE claims should specify what is being investigated, what kinds of evidence can support them, what would count against them, which methods are appropriate to their objects, and under what conditions their scope, formulation, or status should change. The chapter first distinguishes the epistemic status of GRE claims and establishes a modular research architecture. It then formulates research programmes for relational economic structures, allocation, heterogeneous value, value conversion and circulation, generative return, generative spacetime, fast–slow dynamics, economic power, justice, generative exploitation, epistemic economy, and AI-mediated capability asymmetry. These substantive programmes are complemented by domain studies, formal modelling, historical and interpretive inquiry, quantitative and empirical research, comparative theory, institutional experimentation, measurement analysis, counterevidence, negative results, replication, reinterpretation, and research infrastructure. A recurring concern is to prevent operationalization from collapsing the distinctions that motivate GRE. Measurement is therefore treated as a transformation with possible loss and reflexive effects; formalization is treated as task-relative rather than as evidence of ontological commitment; justice research keeps normative premises explicit; power and exploitation require mechanism-level identification rather than inference from asymmetry alone; and cross-domain translation preserves non-equivalence and domain-specific remainders. Failed models, failed translations, null results, counterexamples, and negative evidence are treated as constitutive resources for cumulative research rather than as residuals to be discarded. The chapter concludes by specifying how GRE may interact with neighboring Generative Relational domains while retaining disciplinary containment. Candidate cross-domain structures remain hypotheses for further inquiry rather than presumptive components of a completed general theory. GRE thereby emerges not as a closed theoretical system, but as an open research programme whose concepts, methods, models, and domain claims remain historically situated, empirically answerable, formally inspectable, and institutionally revisable.

items.summary: Rank Access and Closure Depth in the Relation-Layer Cohomology of Token Arenas A refuted conjecture, a refuted mechanism, and two species of invariant harmonic residue     Driven by Dean Kulik October 2026     Abstract A K disj -type relation layer over a token arena assigns cohomology to a graph by declaring which closed loops count as relations. We settle an open problem about such layers and then identify what actually governs them. First, the conjecture that two vertex orbits force ε harm ( K 4 ) = 0 is refuted by an exact 12-vertex counterexample with |Aut| = 24, reproduced by two implementations whose constructions of the invariant cochain space share no logic. Second, we localize the failure: it is not a shortage of cells. On the witness's two-dimensional residue, all 1083 arena 4-cycles supply rank 1, while 20 arena 3-cycles of an excluded shape supply rank 2, and the two nonzero square families have the same image, a single line. Third, we refute the natural mechanism for this — that the residue is an odd-cycle blind spot — by exhibiting bipartite arenas, containing no odd cycle of any length, that still carry residue. The operative property is omission from the declared family, not parity. Fourth, we prove that ε harm ( K 3,4 ) > 0 on an infinite family — every cycle graph with n ≥ 5 and 2 ≤ K ≤ n−1, under the trivial group and the rotation subgroup, and zero under the full dihedral group — answering a question the odd-cycle reading had posed. Fifth, we define closure depth L closure , prove it exceeds 4 for every member of that family, and measure it as exactly n for C n and 4 for the witness, so no short vocabulary closes the family. This separates two populated regimes: residue a longer reader dissolves, and residue carried by configuration-space topology. Finally we identify the second kind. At trivial group the framework's own quantity is simplicial H 1 over ℚ , and the declared cells are the 2-skeleton of Abrams' discretized configuration space; the cell counts and Euler characteristic are verified against closed form, Abrams' subdivision hypothesis for C n reduces to n ≥ K + 1, the measured rank is 1 on all 33 admissible rows and 0 on all 8 excluded boundary rows, and the equivariant degree is solved exactly: +1 for rotations, −1 for reflections. All arithmetic is exact rational. One is obtained by declaring a relation layer: a set of closed loops in some derived space that are stipulated to bound. Change the declaration and the cohomology changes while the graph does not. This paper is about what that dependence actually is, measured rather than described. The derived space here is a token arena . Fix a finite simple graph X , an integer K ≥ 1, and a group G ≤ Aut( X ). The arena A K ( X ) has the K -element subsets of V ( X ) as vertices, with an edge whenever two subsets differ by moving one token along one edge of X . A relation layer declares a family of arena loops as 2-cells; the G -invariant cochain complex of the resulting 2-complex has a first cohomology whose dimension we write ε harm . The quantity is relative to the declaration, and that is the point. Two declarations are natural and were already in use. K disj admits only commuting squares : two token moves along base edges with disjoint closed supports, which therefore commute. K 4 admits every 4-cycle of the arena. items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly construct multi-agent workflows that decompose a complex task and assign specialist agents from a pool. However, building such a workflow well remains challenging: how finely to divide the task, which agent to trust with each subtask, and when to create a new specialist are all critical decisions a workflow constructor needs to settle up front. Thus, whether each subtask succeeds remains unknown until the workflow runs. Yet, improving a workflow is costly. Locating a fault usually requires a reference answer, a graded outcome, or a trained assessor, and the fix is applied to the whole workflow through re-execution, re-search, or retraining. We propose InFlowOp, which prices every decision in one label-free cost that weighs how well an agent's competence meets what a subtask demands against how much that agent takes to run. Before execution, InFlowOp bidirectionally determines the granularity of task decomposition and agent assignment following from the cost rather than from a fixed template. During execution, InFlowOp corrects a fault with the cheapest move via the same cost that serves the workflow both as it is built and as it runs. Facing the workflow-level evaluation challenge, we introduce Braid, a benchmark whose tasks require multi-agent coordination beyond single-agent capability. Across various domains and backbones, InFlowOp outperforms single agent baselines by up to $+11.97\%$, achieving $+9.64\%$ with in-flow optimization. Our project page: https://xhguo7.github.io/InFlowOp/.
items.title: Pay for the Fault, Not the Flow: Label-Free In-Flow Multi-Agent Workflow Optimization

items.summary: This dataset was produced using a harmonised methodology for estimating the spatial distribution of citrus areas across the European Union at 10 × 10 km grid resolution for the 2020 reference year. The approach integrates Eurostat **Farm Structure Survey (FSS) 2020** gridded agricultural statistics, official regional agricultural statistics and the Copernicus High Resolution Layer (HRL) Crop Types. Missing or suppressed FSS values are estimated using regional crop-area totals and Earth Observation-derived spatial weights, while reported values are transferred, aggregated or disaggregated to the common EEA reference grid according to their source resolution. The resulting map provides quantitative citrus-area estimates, crop-presence indicators, provenance metadata and a rule-based methodological uncertainty class for each grid cell. Evaluation against official regional statistics and independent **Land Use/Cover Area Frame Survey (LUCAS)** field observations showed overall consistency with the source statistics and a 95.1% detection rate for LUCAS-positive grid cells. The resulting spatial dataset is intended to support EFSA plant health risk assessment and related spatial analyses.
items.title: Spatial distribution of citrus areas in the European Union at 10 × 10 km grid resolution, 2020

items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist [Data set]. Kaggle. https://doi.org/10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/195341 Official source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce License: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (`CC BY-NC-SA 4.0`).

items.summary: FAIR+D Canon™ V6 Sovereign Financial System & IP Licensing Architecture — Scientific Validation, Controlled Reauthoring, Evidence Integrity, Publication Package & Supplementary Companion Archive Abstract FAIR+D Canon™ V6 is a controlled research, methodological, documentary, computational, and evidentiary framework accompanied by a structured Principal Publication Package and a separately maintained Supplementary Companion Package . The V6 release preserves the documented methodological architecture, controlled reauthoring corpus, standards and protocol documentation, scientific and forensic evidence, source-validation materials, evidentiary boundaries, admissibility decisions, archival integrity records, computational workflow documentation, author and persistent-identifier information, rights and licensing documentation, intellectual-property evidence status, commercial-term evidence status, third-party licensing evidence status, and release-level verification records associated with the documented V6 research state. The release architecture deliberately maintains explicit distinctions between: methodological specification and empirical observation; source-derived information and derived or normalized values; observed data and methodological configuration; scientific evidence and forensic or archival evidence; preservation and scientific admission; historical recovery and new computation or reconstruction; verified identity and unresolved identity; discovery, verification, adjudication, and admission; documentary rights language and independent legal conclusions; preserved supporting material and strictly admissible scientific evidence; and release-level package integrity and substantive scientific validity. items.summary: Berggren's three matrices generate the tree of primitive Pythagorean triples and preserve the quadratic form x₁² + x₂² − x₃². Cha, Nguyen and Tauber (2018) built such trees for other integral ternary forms Q of signature (2,1). We ask whether the matrices alone determine Q. Main results: Recovery criterion (Theorem 3.1). A set of isometries of Q determines Q up to scale exactly when no nonzero vector is sent to plus or minus itself by all of them. Equivalently, the group they generate is not virtually abelian; for integral isometries, it acts irreducibly. The proof is elementary linear algebra and applies to arbitrary real groups. Berggren trees (Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.3, Remark 3.5). Any two generators determine Q in Berggren's tree and in each of the five trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber. The definition of a Berggren tree alone does not force this: the generators A and A² give a Berggren forest for x₁² + x₂² − x₃² whose two generators both yield edges but do not determine Q. Roots at a rational null line (Theorem 3.6). For a primitive null vector P with divisor G, the minimum of Q on (P^⊥ ∩ ℤ³) \ ℤP is S = |det(2J)|/(2G²). An explicit congruence, Gm ≡ −τ (mod S), decides which minimal vectors e + mP are roots. N-cusps (Theorems 3.7–3.8, Corollary 3.9). For Q = ax₁² + bx₁x₂ + cx₂² − Nx₃² with D = b² − 4ac < 0, all data at the null vectors (p, q, 1) are explicit. A minimal root exists there if and only if gcd(G, S) divides D/G, and in particular whenever D is cube-free. Recovery by integral reflections (Theorem 3.12, Proposition 3.13). Minimal roots at two or three distinct rational null lines yield three integral reflections that determine Q. The paper also relates the reflections in the trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber to minimal roots (Remark 3.17), and states an open question for trees produced by their construction.
items.title: The Inverse Berggren Tree Problem

items.summary: This chapter develops the research programme of Generative Relational Economics (GRE) by translating the conceptual, methodological, and substantive architectures developed earlier in the book into a cumulative, contestable, and revisable programme of inquiry. Its principal concern is answerability: GRE claims should specify what is being investigated, what kinds of evidence can support them, what would count against them, which methods are appropriate to their objects, and under what conditions their scope, formulation, or status should change. The chapter first distinguishes the epistemic status of GRE claims and establishes a modular research architecture. It then formulates research programmes for relational economic structures, allocation, heterogeneous value, value conversion and circulation, generative return, generative spacetime, fast–slow dynamics, economic power, justice, generative exploitation, epistemic economy, and AI-mediated capability asymmetry. These substantive programmes are complemented by domain studies, formal modelling, historical and interpretive inquiry, quantitative and empirical research, comparative theory, institutional experimentation, measurement analysis, counterevidence, negative results, replication, reinterpretation, and research infrastructure. A recurring concern is to prevent operationalization from collapsing the distinctions that motivate GRE. Measurement is therefore treated as a transformation with possible loss and reflexive effects; formalization is treated as task-relative rather than as evidence of ontological commitment; justice research keeps normative premises explicit; power and exploitation require mechanism-level identification rather than inference from asymmetry alone; and cross-domain translation preserves non-equivalence and domain-specific remainders. Failed models, failed translations, null results, counterexamples, and negative evidence are treated as constitutive resources for cumulative research rather than as residuals to be discarded. The chapter concludes by specifying how GRE may interact with neighboring Generative Relational domains while retaining disciplinary containment. Candidate cross-domain structures remain hypotheses for further inquiry rather than presumptive components of a completed general theory. GRE thereby emerges not as a closed theoretical system, but as an open research programme whose concepts, methods, models, and domain claims remain historically situated, empirically answerable, formally inspectable, and institutionally revisable.

items.summary: Reproducing a machine-learning result requires knowing how the experiment was run: the data, the model and its size, the optimiser, the learning rate, the batch size, the number of steps, the hardware and the seeds. This information is scattered through a paper---often only in a table caption or an appendix---and is increasingly extracted automatically by language-model pipelines, whose evaluations report how often they are right. We ask the two questions those evaluations leave open: when a pipeline is wrong, does it know it is wrong; and how much human effort does it take to find out? We build a benchmark of 80 arXiv machine-learning papers and annotate 24 of them (240 field decisions), 12 of them through two independent annotation passes, carrying verbatim, line-numbered evidence for every reported and every absent field; the passes agree on 97.5% of presence/absence decisions (Cohen's κ = 0.94), and the residual disagreements are adjudicated under a written scope rule. On that gold standard we run six extraction conditions of increasing agency---a single untruncated prompt, a tool-using agent, schema constraints, table/appendix re-reading, per-field self-assessment with a suspect flag, and mandatory evidence back-linking---over three difficulty strata, 432 full-paper extractions in total. Four results. First, agency buys no accuracy: present recall varies by one percentage point across all six conditions (0.883–0.894) while wall-clock time varies threefold. Second, honesty is a different quantity: 92% of the 387 wrong values were returned without any indication of doubt, and the share of returned values that are silently wrong falls from 12.7% to 5.5% only in the condition asked to flag its own doubts; requiring an evidence quote for every value restores the silent rate to 11.2% because it crowds out the doubt flag. Third, the errors are not inventions: every returned value that carries a checkable anchor occurs somewhere in the paper, and 375 of the 387 errors are values the document does contain—misattributions that belong to another configuration, another table, or the reference list, or values lifted from elsewhere in the paper—which is why a gold-standard-free anchor audit detects none of them (we report that as a negative result, with the five PDF text-layer artefacts it originally fired on pinned as a 22-case regression test). Fourth, human verification is the binding cost and it is predictable: verifying one field by hand requires a median of 12 candidate passages (up to 273; 4,707 in total for the gold sample) against one passage with an evidence link, although 4 of 25 spot-checked links failed adjudication, three of them because the quoted line does not hold the value. All corpus, prompts, gold annotations, adjudication records, raw runs, per-item API costs and analysis scripts are released with the paper, together with a per-session cost ledger ( runs/session-costs.json : the grid itself cost $2.84, the 644 sessions recorded in the released artefacts cost $3.22).

items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). items.summary: Data and Python code accompanying the manuscript “Replication-Based Criteria Can Change the Selected Number of Clusters: A Seven-Criterion Audit of k-Means on Indonesian Provincial Environmental Data” (submitted to the Journal of Computing Theories and Applications). The package audits how the number of clusters, k, is selected for k-means on a small tabular dataset: the published components of Indonesia’s Environmental Quality Index (Indeks Kualitas Lingkungan Hidup) for 38 provinces, 2021–2024. Seven criteria are computed for k = 2 to 8: the within-cluster sum of squares (read visually and by two formal knee rules), silhouette width, the Davies–Bouldin and Calinski–Harabasz indices, the gap statistic, subsample stability (adjusted Rand index over 200 pairs of overlapping 80% subsamples) and agreement with Ward linkage. The scripts also run sensitivity analyses, a comparison of six clustering algorithms, fixed-centroid assignment across years, a leave-one-out comparison of regression models for the air quality component, permutation importance and exact Shapley values. Contents: data/ (index components 2021–2024; GRDP per capita and population density; a cell-level provenance audit), code/ (six analysis scripts and a plotting-style module), README.md (run order, variable dictionary and data sources), requirements.txt (pinned library versions), CITATION.cff and licence files. Running the six scripts in the order given in README.md reproduces every table and figure of the manuscript in about four minutes on a laptop (Python 3.11 or later). The indicator values are official statistics from Statistics Indonesia (Badan Pusat Statistik) and are reproduced unchanged. Please cite the original BPS tables as well as this record. Code: MIT licence. Data files: CC BY 4.0.

items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
items.title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks

items.summary: Code and text-free reproducibility artifacts for the manuscript “Saudi Arabic Automatic Speech Recognition and Dialect Identification Using Calibrated System Combination and Gated Multimodal Fusion,” currently under revision at Scientific Reports . The repository implements a Saudi Arabic automatic speech recognition framework using XLSR-53, XLS-R 300M, XLS-R 1B, and MMS-1B with validation-tuned KenLM decoding, evaluation under a dialect-normalized scoring convention applied to both references and hypotheses, and calibrated N-best system combination. The reproduced combined test WER is 32.49% , compared with 34.04% for the best single-model configuration. XLSR-53 was evaluated on a 1,652-utterance subset of the test set and is therefore treated as an indicative baseline. The repository also provides SaudiDID-X, a multimodal Saudi dialect identification framework using frozen multi-layer MMS-1B acoustic representations and frozen SaudiBERT text features with a residual adapter and gated fusion. The audio-only comparison is the acoustic branch of the same SaudiDID-X training run , not an independently trained model. The archived test macro-F1 values are 52.01% for the audio-only branch and 53.79% for SaudiDID-X. The release includes analysis and reference-training notebooks, configuration metadata, anonymized split identifiers, text-free per-utterance result artifacts, statistical-test outputs, figures, tables, checksums, and a verification script. Raw audio and third-party transcriptions are not redistributed because of source-specific licensing restrictions. v1.0.2: Documentation, provenance, and configuration-metadata corrections. Archived predictions, primary reported metrics, data splits, checksums, and computational implementation are unchanged. See CHANGELOG.md for the complete list of corrections. v1.0.1: Configuration-metadata corrections for the single-run reporting protocol and per-stage training hyperparameters. No result values changed.

items.summary: Privacy-derived scientific materials for controlled studies of evidence access and adverse product content in AI assessment. The supplement contains synthetic materials, prompts, recorded model answers, terminal failures, assignment mappings, original stage-specific scoring and statistical implementations, reference results, and an offline CPU replay entrypoint. It includes the main local studies, the hosted-model study, historical screening, two common-interface qualification rounds, and the exploratory two-model pilot. Screening and development records are kept distinct from formal comparisons; reused answer aliases are not independent generations. The qualification amendment was made after qualification and before the exploratory pilot, and the subsequent proposed formal extension was not run. The findings do not establish a general advantage of pre-event defense, equivalence, or broad robustness. This is a redacted scientific derivative with a new integrity manifest: account authorizations, user dialogue, machine paths, hardware logs, original provider envelopes, encrypted reasoning, native token journals and model weights are excluded. CPU replay reproduces scores and statistics from the released scientific records; it does not regenerate answers or repeat the original private token/authorization/environment audits.
